gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a 3-channel camera's headline front resolution is a camera-off mode: Vantrue's own listing gives the OnDash N4 4K only as "Single Front 4K (2160P@25fps)" and 1440P+1080P+1080P at 30 fps with all three recording, and Redtiger's own F17 listing says to "turn off the inside camera to enable 4K front and 1080P rear recording".
standout_why: I compared seven result pages. Digital Camera World's budget guide (cited) showed only 1- and 2-channel cameras in the part I could read, and says only that parking mode needs hardwiring. Walmart's 3-channel browse page (cited) returned a bot wall, so I could not read it. Dash & Drive's under-$100 page has no 3-channel camera and estimates "another $20 to $30" for a hardwire kit. Deal.ai's 3-channel list has the N4 at $99.99 and the Redtiger A3 at $72.74, with nothing on three-camera versus front-only resolution or on hardwire kits. my-best's 3-channel page comes closest: it gives one resolution per N4 camera (1440P front and inside, 1080P rear) with a "Dual recording mode" footnote, and says three cameras store about 10 hours of full HD. None says the 4K figure applies only with the other cameras off, quotes the maker on it, or prices the N4's hardwire kit. I did not open Car and Driver, TechRadar, MotorTrend, Product Bible, Dash Cam Empire or the second chat's other results.
decides: It confirms the Vantrue OnDash N4 belongs on the page at $99.99 (Vantrue's store, 2026-11-26), but removes "4K" as a reason to pick it. With front, cabin and rear all recording it is 1440P+1080P+1080P at 30 fps, the same tier Redtiger states for the $72.74 A3 (2.5K+1080P+1080P). The choice between them therefore rests on other things: the sensor each maker names, GPS, Wi-Fi and price. It also keeps the Redtiger F17 out on two counts: $129.99 is over the line, and its 4K front needs the cabin camera off. Parking mode pushes the N4 past $100: the cheapest Vantrue hardwire kit whose listing names the N4 is $29.99, so $129.98 together.
